subject: Day 70: confirm caregiver Tdap
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 10 weeks into the calmest stretch of year one, so this is the week to harden the systems around him. Today's lead item is cocooning: make sure every adult who holds him is current on their own vaccines.

Action items
- Confirm that grandparents and any nanny are current on Tdap, MMR, flu, and COVID per the CDC adult schedule before they hold Avi. Pertussis is the contact illness most likely to kill an infant, and adult boosters are the primary defense for a baby this young. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Build a childcare backup plan now: identify a backup nanny agency or an on-call family member before a sick day forces the question. Care.com: https://www.care.com/
- Inquire about first-birthday venues if you want a formal event; top SF and NYC venues book six to nine months out.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Sleep stretches that lengthen one week and shorten the next. Week-to-week variability in the longest night stretch is normal in the 8-to-14-week window.
- [monitor] Persistent fisted hands that never open, or movement that consistently favors one side; note it and raise at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A new feeding-refusal pattern, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips or labored breathing, or a limp, unresponsive episode. Call the pediatrician same-day for fever; call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Confirm the adult-vaccine cocoon as part of social safety: the people in Avi's daily orbit are his pertussis firewall, so log each caregiver's Tdap date. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Place an unbreakable mirror in front of Avi during tummy time to motivate head lift; aim for 60 to 75 minutes per day cumulative across short bouts. HealthyChildren tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Extend his cooing exchanges by responding to each vocalization, pausing, then answering the next. This serve-and-return cadence predicts later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; start anchoring a consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (4-month visit): RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
